title: Chemical potentials from structure factors: I. Neutral multi-component mixtures
abstract:
arXiv:2608.08357v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The chemical potentials of multi-component mixtures underlie many physical and chemical phenomena, but remain challenging to compute. The S0 method enables the computation of chemical potentials from equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations, by leveraging the thermodynamic relationship between particle number fluctuations and derivatives of chemical potentials, followed by numerical integration along different compositions. Here we generalize the S0 method from two-component mixtures to neutral multi-component mixtures. We first extend the statistical mechanical formalism to high-dimensional compositional space, and then introduce a Gaussian process integration scheme combined with active learning to efficiently integrate chemical potentials and sample diverse compositions. We use this method to compute the mixing free energies of a molten metal alloy, and the solubilities of two paracetamol polymorphs in water-ethanol solvents. The extended S0 method provides a practical and scalable route for computing chemical potentials in neutral bulk multi-component mixtures from atomistic simulations.
relevance_reason: Key author: Bingqing Cheng

title: Chemical potentials from structure factors: II. Charged multi-component mixtures
abstract:
arXiv:2608.30060v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The chemical potentials of charged multi-component mixtures are central to electrolyte thermodynamics, but remain difficult to compute from atomistic simulations. The S0 method enables computing chemical potentials of mixtures from equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations. Here we extend the S0 method to charged mixtures by combining the composition-space framework developed in Part I: Neutral Multi-component Mixtures with a Coulombic treatment of the small-wavenumber limits of static structure factors. This approach separates thermodynamically relevant neutral composition fluctuations from forbidden macroscopic charge fluctuations, and further accounts for charge-neutrality constraints. We use the method to compute the chemical potentials of multiple-halide aqueous salt solutions, elucidating the ion-specific thermodynamic effects. We also calculate the mixing free energies of molten salt mixtures, demonstrating the importance of correctly describing long-wavelength electrostatic correlations.
relevance_reason: Key author: Bingqing Cheng

title: Few-Step Boltzmann Generators via Scalable Likelihood Flow Maps
abstract:
arXiv:2606.29110v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recent progress in flow-based generative modeling has led to models that output high-quality samples while using only a small number of function evaluations. However, at present, there is a lack of similar advances in estimating the model likelihood. In particular, most existing methods either rely on restrictive architectures that enable exact calculations, or use stochastic approximations such as Hutchinson's trace estimator that introduce substantial variance. In this work, we introduce SCAlable LikeLihood distillation of flOw maPs (SCALLOP). SCALLOP builds on the recently proposed F2D2, a likelihood flow map model that can generate samples and their densities in a small number of function evaluations. While F2D2 uses Hutchinson's estimator during training, we introduce an alternative and more scalable likelihood distillation objective that is Hutchinson-free and admits a vectorized formulation. Empirically, we demonstrate the effectiveness of SCALLOP as a Boltzmann generator in molecular science, and further validate its benefit on image datasets. SCALLOP significantly reduces both training variance and training time while consistently improving performance compared to F2D2, and is competitive with the state-of-the-art while achieving up to 10x inference speedup over the fastest baseline.

title: When do machine-learning potentials need a configuration-dependent kernel? Learning long-range interactions with Fourier neural operators
abstract:
arXiv:2611.03678v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Long-range interactions in machine-learning interatomic potentials are commonly treated by coupling learned sources through either a prescribed electrostatic kernel or a learned but configuration-independent one. Whether such a kernel suffices depends on the underlying screened interaction. We address this question by using Fourier neural operators (FNOs) to learn how latent source fields, built from the descriptors of a local backbone (here MACE), interact across the simulation cell. For a synthetic ionic system with tunable screening, a prescribed Coulomb kernel underestimates the long-wavelength charge fluctuations by 43% under strong screening, whereas the FNO reproduces them within 3% and recovers 95-99% of the variance of the residual left by the local backbone. A linear FNO, which learns a configuration-independent kernel, performs equally well in the homogeneous case. Under inhomogeneous screening, rearranging the remote medium modulates the coupling between distant ions, a dependence that no configuration-independent kernel can represent. Among the models tested, only the nonlinear FNO responds to this modulation, and its force errors are 27-41% lower than those of configuration-independent models. In first-principles benchmarks of liquid water, lithium lanthanum zirconate, and Au2/MgO(001), MACE-FNO is comparable to a prescribed-kernel model for the bulk systems and more accurate for the interface. It further captures the reversal of the Au2 wetting preference induced by remote Al dopants, with deviations below 5 meV per cell from density functional theory. These results indicate that a configuration-dependent kernel, as learned by FNOs, becomes necessary once the screening medium varies, even though the energy remains quadratic in the charges for a fixed medium.
relevance_reason: Develops and benchmarks a MACE-FNO machine-learned interatomic potential with explicit atoms and force/energy validation, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Isothermal-Isobaric Molecular Dynamics with a Foundation Interatomic Potential in LAMMPS across NVIDIA and Intel GPUs
abstract:
arXiv:2611.03892v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer one model for many chemistries, but their deep, globally coupled architectures do not fit the spatial decomposition that scales classical and short-ranged MLIPs. We present pair_style uma, a LAMMPS pair style that evaluates the Universal Model for Atoms (UMA) through LibTorch on NVIDIA and Intel GPUs from a single source tree. It reimplements FairChem's edge-sharded graph parallelism in C++ over exported TorchScript modules, with one MPI rank per device, NCCL or oneCCL collectives, and the whole energy and force path in double precision. The strain-gradient virial is carried through the exported modules and the cross-device reductions, so that fix npt runs on both vendors' hardware. We measure NPT capacity and cost on one 4xA100-40GB node, one 8xH200 node, and one 12-tile Intel node, and on up to 32 Intel nodes. Without activation checkpointing, one node holds NaCl cells of about 8,000 atoms (A100, 0.21 ns/day), 22,000 atoms (Intel, 0.10 ns/day), and 47,000 atoms (H200, 0.16 ns/day). Graph parallelism raises the capacity of a single device by 8.0x on H200 and 4.6x on A100. Across nodes, capacity grows to about 779,000 atoms on 32 Intel nodes, with a slower speed at 0.007 ns/day. On H200 and A100, a FLOP count of FairChem's graph-parallel predictor gives lower bounds of 31% and 51% of FP64 peak. From one omat checkpoint and with no refit, nine 100 ps NPT heating ramps (NaCl, equiatomic Pt-Ru, and equiatomic (HfNbTaTiZr)N, on all three node types) ran to completion.
relevance_reason: LAMMPS pair style for the UMA foundation MLIP with NPT molecular dynamics benchmarked across NVIDIA/Intel GPUs; explicit-atom MD driven by a machine-learned potential satisfies (a)-(c) directly.

title: Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Reveals Grotthuss Transport in Concentrated Electrolytes
abstract:
arXiv:2611.04558v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Proton transfer is responsible for the anomalous high conductivity in acidic or basic aqueous solutions. Yet, the contribution of the proton transfer mechanism to the conductivity of concentrated aqueous solutions is unknown. In this work, we compute the transport properties of KOH(aq) systems with different concentrations, using Molecular Dynamics simulations with a Machine Learning Interatomic Potential (MLIP), which includes proton transfer. We quantify the contribution of the proton transfer mechanism to the diffusivities of hydroxide ions and water molecules, and the ionic conductivity and transport numbers of the electrolytes. The contribution is substantial at lower concentrations, but diminishes at very high concentrations.
relevance_reason: Machine-learned interatomic potential MD of KOH(aq) electrolytes including proton transfer to compute diffusivities, conductivities and transport numbers; explicit-atom MLIP-driven simulation satisfies (a)-(c).

title: TT-SCHA for Thermodynamics of Binary Alloys
abstract:
arXiv:2611.04402v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The free energy of a crystal is an integral over the positions of all its atoms, in 3N dimensions. We evaluate it without random sampling for the ordered alloys B2 NiAl and gamma-TiAl with embedded-atom potentials, using a self-consistent harmonic approximation (SCHA) corrected to third order in temperature, calculated via thermal averages of tensor-train (TT) integrals built from one atom and its neighbors, which we call TT-SCHA. The result is for an infinite crystal without sampling error; its numerical error is set by the starting pivots of the interpolation (up to 9 MPa in the pressure, reduced by averaging three runs; SM Table S26). Against the molecular dynamics of 65,536 atoms (Frenkel-Ladd free energy at 600 K, integrated energy above), TT-SCHA free energy agrees to 0.13 meV per atom at 600-1000 K, using 420-500 times fewer core-seconds for one run. At zero pressure, results agree with published calculations that use the same embedded-atom potential: the published elastic constants of gamma-TiAl (to 1 GPa, by a static lattice calculation) and its thermal expansion from Monte Carlo sampling (to 0.012 percentage points).
relevance_reason: Computes alloy free energies with EAM potentials using TT-SCHA and validates against large-scale molecular dynamics, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Benchmarking and advancing machine-learning interatomic potentials for 3C-SiC across equilibrium and extreme conditions
abstract:
arXiv:2510.06966v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Several machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have been developed for cubic silicon carbide (3C-SiC). Here, we benchmark seven existing MLIPs against a common set of structural, thermal, defect, radiation-damage, disordered-phase, and computational-performance tests. We also introduce two complementary MLIPs trained on DFT-labeled crystalline, liquid, amorphous, and defective configurations. TGAP, a Gaussian approximation potential based on the \verb|soap_turbo| descriptor, provides consistently high accuracy across the sampled configurational space. MTP, a custom moment tensor potential, retains good accuracy across these regimes while offering substantially lower computational cost, GPU acceleration, and access to multi-million-atom simulations. As an application-level test, both potentials remain stable in displacement cascades spanning short-range repulsion, transient disorder, and recrystallization. Overall, MTP emerges as a particularly strong accuracy--cost compromise for large-scale and strongly non-equilibrium simulations of 3C-SiC.
relevance_reason: Explicit benchmarking and training of machine-learned interatomic potentials (GAP/SOAP, MTP) for 3C-SiC with DFT-labeled configurations and MD-based radiation-damage tests, satisfying (a), (b) MLIP development/benchmarking, and (c).

title: Next generation of ultra-coarse-graining: Self-consistent inference of critical internal states
abstract: Bottom-up coarse-graining systematically expands the length and effective timescales accessible to molecular dynamics simulations, but the information loss during coarse-graining can prevent an accurate incorporation of the multistate phenomena common in complex biomolecular dynamics. The Ultra-Coarse-Graining (UCG) method projects the influence of discrete “quantum-like” extended degrees of freedom, “internal states,” onto the coarse-grained (CG) mapped molecules, significantly extending the expressiveness of the CG model. The previous rapid-local-equilibrium (RLE) approximation in UCG depends on user-defined collective variables (CVs, e.g., local density) and does not incorporate correlations between internal states within and between CG molecules. We present Self-Consistent UCG (SC-UCG), an integrated methodology that utilizes the underlying UCG interactions directly for internal state designation, without designing collective variables in the CG ensemble. For simulations, the internal state probabilities are self-consistently determined via graph message-passing in simulation time. We also enhance the RLE Hamiltonian with the Bethe approximation plus AI-based inference to allow explicit internal state correlations between UCG beads. For forcefield training, we develop Multilayer Internal State Consistency, a machine-learning-based method derived from the relative entropy minimization principle that does not require iterative sampling of the intermediate forcefields. We then apply SC-UCG to a model tetramer system with a second-order symmetry-breaking phase transition from the supercritical racemic fluid into subcritical D-rich and L-rich fluids. We show that SC-UCG can capture collective switching events of internal UCG states in the subcritical region, and it exhibits temperature transferability by recapitulating the phase transition, even if trained from a single-temperature dataset.
relevance_reason: Develops self-consistent ultra-coarse-graining with MD simulations and ML force-field training, satisfying (a) CG beads with atomistic mapping, (b) CG MD and force-field development, and (c) method advance.

title: Bicarbonate/carbonic acid equilibria in aqueous solutions: Conformational Dynamics, Ion-Pair Speciation, and Free Energy Landscapes from Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics and Metadynamics
abstract:
arXiv:2611.04121v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Carbonic acid (H2CO3) is connected with the dissolved CO2 and bicarbonate (HCO3-) equilibria in aqueous solutions. Its two elementary reactions in water, acid dissociation and dehydration to CO2, are difficult to resolve because both are coupled to proton transfer through hydrogen-bonded networks. In this work, we combine 0.5 ns of unbiased PBE-D3 molecular dynamics of 1 molar solution of H2CO3 with metadynamics on the O - H coordination (H2CO3 = HCO3- + H+) and the C - O distance of the leaving hydroxyl (H2CO3 <=> CO2 + H2O). These unbiased trajectories show frequent cis-cis <=> cis-trans interconversion through long-lived bicarbonate (well separated from solvated proton, H3O+, and also mediated by a short-lived three-water [H2O...H3O+...H2O] ring that acts as a solvent-shared ion pair (SSIP); only 16-23% of deprotonation events reach a solvent-separated ion pair (SShIP). Resolving ion-pairs as SSIP for proper reaction leads to an improved estimate of pKa1 from 1.1 to 2.4, toward the experimental 3.45-3.59 (measured at supposedly infinite dilution). Further, metadynamics simulations provide a dehydration barrier of 17.8 (1D) and 15.3 kcal/mol (2D), suggesting that the final product CO2 + H2O is 2.8 kcal/mol below H2CO3. Our two-dimensional free energy surface also shows that C--O cleavage proceeds through the CO2 + OH- which further goes down by 9.9 kcal/mol to product CO2 + H2O.
relevance_reason: Ab initio (PBE-D3) molecular dynamics combined with 1D/2D metadynamics to obtain pKa, ion-pair speciation and free-energy landscapes for bicarbonate/carbonic acid; explicit-atom AIMD plus enhanced sampling fully satisfies (a)-(c).

title: Molecular rotor in copper borozene Cu 4 B 8 : A freely rotating σ-aromatic tetrahedral Cu 4  core atop a boron wheel
abstract: We identify two-layered Cu4B8 clusters featuring tetrahedral Cu4 units anchored on B8 boron wheels as global minima. A substantial charge transfer from Cu4 to the B8 wheel is observed, resulting in a charge distribution close to the idealized [Cu42+] [B82−] electron-counting scheme. AdNDP analysis reveals two delocalized σ-electrons within the quasi-tetrahedral Cu4 unit, identifying it as one of the simplest σ-aromatic motifs. The B82− wheels exhibit dual (6π + 6σ) aromaticity, serving as boron analogs of benzene (“borozene”). Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics simulations show pronounced fluxionality, with nearly barrierless Cu4 rotation (∼0.01 kcal/mol) enabled by an ultrasoft vibrational mode. The delocalized electronic structure of the B8 wheel contributes to the facile Cu4 rotation, while electrostatic and dative interactions stabilize the two-layer framework. These results identify electroneutral Cu4B8 as a prototypical copper–borozene cluster combining aromatic stabilization and dynamic fluxionality, offering a promising model for molecular rotor.
relevance_reason: This performs DFT global-minimum searches and Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics on explicit Cu4B8 clusters, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) BOMD/DFT, and (c) mechanistic application to cluster fluxionality.

title: GW  reduced density matrix from iterated linearized Dyson equation
abstract: Iterating the Dyson equation with the static part of the self-energy leads to a concise and possibly improved expression of the one-body reduced density matrix from any self-energy approximation. Here, we apply the procedure to Hedin’s GW approximation. The non-iterated GW-based density matrix was already known to yield accurate density matrices for molecular systems. We show that the Dyson-equation-based procedure is equivalent to the so-called variational Z-vector approach applied to the random-phase approximation energy functional, but only in the case of a Hartree–Fock mean-field starting point. When a generalized Kohn–Sham scheme is employed instead, the two approaches differ. By comparing the density matrix for a benchmark set of 34 small molecules to coupled-cluster reference values, we conclude that the iterated Dyson equation indeed produces improved density matrices for molecular systems. Interestingly, we observe that the excitation rank of the reference coupled-cluster matters much and that the inclusion of triple excitations quantitatively changes the conclusions of the benchmark compared to single and double excitations coupled-cluster.
relevance_reason: This is GW/electronic-structure method development for molecular reduced density matrices benchmarked against coupled cluster, satisfying (a) explicit molecular atoms, (b) post-HF/GW quantum-chemistry methodology, and (c) method advance.

title: Vibrational spectra and anharmonic coupling of the O–H stretch in 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline: Insights from constrained nuclear–electronic orbital theory
abstract: Hydrogen bonds can exhibit pronounced nuclear quantum effects (NQEs) that strongly influence proton-transfer dynamics. 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline (HBQ) is a prototypical excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) system with a strong intramolecular hydrogen bond, and its vibrational spectra and anharmonic mode couplings have recently attracted considerable interest. Here, we use constrained nuclear–electronic orbital density functional theory (CNEO-DFT) and molecular dynamics (CNEO-MD), which account for NQEs, particularly nuclear quantum delocalization effects, to investigate the O–H stretching vibration (νOH) of HBQ and its anharmonic coupling with other modes in the ground state. The νOH frequency calculated by CNEO-DFT agrees closely with the experiment, and CNEO-MD reproduces the characteristic finger-like structure of the infrared spectrum. Normal mode frequency shift analysis and CNEO-MD simulations with resonant νOH excitation consistently identify several low-frequency in-plane backbone bending modes that are strongly coupled to the νOH. Taken together, this work establishes a detailed understanding of the ground-state vibrational spectrum and νOH mode couplings in HBQ, providing a basis for further investigation of their roles in ESIPT dynamics.
relevance_reason: This uses CNEO-DFT and CNEO-MD with explicit atoms to study vibrational spectra and anharmonic coupling, satisfying (a) atomistic representation, (b) DFT-based molecular dynamics, and (c) application to a molecular system.

title: samQEq: universal charge equilibration for molecules and conductors
abstract:
arXiv:2611.03687v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Charge equilibration assigns atomic charges by equalizing an atomic chemical potential built from electronegativity, hardness and the Coulomb interaction. Under one global constraint it lets charge flow without limit between molecules, which fluctuating-charge models prevent with one neutrality constraint per molecule. A metal needs the opposite: a global constraint and a hardness near zero, and there the charge operator becomes indefinite unless it includes each charge's own self-energy. Here, we present samQEq (solids-and-molecules QEq), a unified charge-equilibration package for LAMMPS that combines the two constructions in one energy functional and one matrix-free solve. An orthogonal projector imposes one neutrality constraint per molecule, and the finite-width self-energy of a Gaussian charge on designated conductor types, narrower than the conductor's own Gaussian, keeps the conductor's part of the operator positive definite at any hardness. On a gold slab carrying a water film, the operator stays definite down to the conductor limit of the model, the metal screens a point charge by a constant amount at every height beyond 4 {\AA}, and the film's charges stay bounded under dynamics. Reciprocal-space electrostatics is evaluated inside the matrix-vector product, and three distinct shielding kernels are run-time settings. We verify the implementation by reproducing a published fluctuating-charge water model without refitting, and the native ReaxFF charge-equilibration step to approximately $10^{-9}\,e$. On a single four-V100 node the largest tested systems run at approximately twice the throughput of a 128-core CPU node. samQEq thus provides one charge-equilibration layer for molecules, conductors and the interfaces between them.
relevance_reason: Development and implementation of a charge-equilibration (fluctuating-charge) model for LAMMPS validated on a gold slab with a water film under dynamics; this is classical force-field/electrostatics method development satisfying (a), (b) and (c).

title: Statistically Robust Characterization of Polaron and Bipolaron Intrinsic Traps in Amorphous Silica Reveals the Role of Network Flexibility in Electron Localisation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.04652v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Intrinsic electron localization in amorphous silica (a-SiO2) contributes to charge trapping and defect generation in silica-based electronic materials - a phenomenon that degrades logic-device performance but can be exploited for memory applications. However, the structural distribution of one- and two-electron traps remains incompletely characterized, largely because the disordered covalent network of a-SiO2 spans a vast configurational space. To address this, we perform statistical sampling to select a representative 200-model subset of defect-free bulk a-SiO2 structures from a structurally converged parent set of 2512 models, generated via classical melt-quench molecular dynamics simulations. We then characterize the intrinsic one- and two-electron traps in this subset using HSE06 density functional theory calculations. Analysis of neutral precursor sites shows that trapping propensity is not determined by a universal O-Si-O angle or Si-O bond length; it is controlled by the accessibility of the relaxed trap geometry, requiring both local strain and medium-range network flexibility. Single electrons predominantly form edge-centred polarons on distorted SiO4 tetrahedra, with occupied states 3.1-4.3 eV below the conduction band minimum. Injection of a second electron drives stronger lattice relaxation, most commonly Si-O bond elongation leading to rupture, thereby forming threefold-coordinated-Si (Si3) bipolarons and, in some cases, Si-Si-bonded bipolaron configurations. The calculated bipolaron energy ranges are consistent with optical absorption features at 3.7, 4.7, and 6.4 eV associated with intrinsic electron localization.
relevance_reason: Classical melt-quench MD generates 2512 a-SiO2 models followed by HSE06 DFT characterization of polaron/bipolaron traps, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MD+DFT, and (c) applying these methods to elucidate trapping physics.

title: Magnetic ground states of CrPS$_4$ and NiPS$_3$ monolayers from long-range exchange interactions
authors: Herr S. J. van der Zant
abstract:
arXiv:2607.20631v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We investigate the magnetic properties of monolayer CrPS$_4$ and NiPS$_3$ by combining first-principles calculations, second-principles spin models, and Monte Carlo simulations. Unlike conventional approaches that truncate exchange interactions after only a few shells and determine them by fitting total energies, we extract the magnetic exchange tensors directly from density functional theory using the LKAG formalism and include interactions until numerical convergence is achieved. We show that long-range exchange interactions qualitatively modify the magnetic behavior of both materials. In CrPS$_4$, they destabilize the previously predicted ferromagnetic ground state and stabilize a spin-spiral phase, reducing the critical temperature to about 21\,K, in agreement with available experiments. The resulting magnetic phase diagram contains multiple collinear and non-collinear phases that can be tuned by temperature and external magnetic fields. In NiPS$_3$, the experimentally observed zigzag antiferromagnetic order only emerges when exchange interactions up to the fifth shell are included. These results demonstrate that quantitatively predictive spin models for thiophosphate monolayers require long-range exchange interactions and provide a predictive framework for accurately describing two-dimensional van der Waals magnets.
relevance_reason: DFT-derived long-range exchange tensors combined with second-principles spin Hamiltonians and Monte Carlo simulations for CrPS4/NiPS3 monolayers satisfy (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT plus MC on atomic spin configurations, and (c) a predictive magnetic phase-diagram application.
